why: An estimated date (RD:Pro) may widen how far apart two dates can be and still agree; it may never make a MISMATCH score above a MATCH (operator ruling 2026-10-19, "Fix this"; compare-spec 2.21.0, eidr-core 0.69.0). Two sibling Episodes, identical except year-only release dates one year apart (2019 / 2020) with the submitted date flagged estimated. Until 2.21.0 the year path MULTIPLIED the gap-1 credit by DATE_ESTIMATED_LENIENCY (0.57 x 2, capped at 1.0), so this pair scored release_date 1.00 while the same pair with an exact year match scores the Episode gap-0 credit, 0.80 -- the inversion DATE_PROFILES exist to prevent. Now the GAP is divided by the leniency and the table read at 0.5 by interpolation: 0.685. `field_quality_max` 0.79 is the lesson: strictly below the 2.21.0 Episode year-match credit (0.80), so it also refuses a port that rounds the halved gap down to 0 and hands out the match credit itself; if a retune moves that credit, re-derive the bound from it. `field_quality_min` 0.57 is the companion property from the same ruling -- an estimated pair never scores below the same gap unflagged -- and it keeps the max from passing vacuously on a field that left the denominator. Mutation-tested: restoring the credit multiplication fails this pair (1.00 > 0.79) and only this pair; eidr-core 0.68.1 (spec 2.20.0) fails it the same way. SCOPE: the year-level path only. The full-date band and fall-through paths ignored the leniency entirely before 2.21.0 (no inversion there, only a wrong ' est'), and the ' est' detail is not in the invariant vocabulary, so neither is pinned here. No Alt ID, so nothing but the date separates the two scores.
